description:
Mechanism for asserting that multiple OIDC provider accounts (LF SSO, GitHub, GSuite, live.com, etc.) belong to the same person. Three linking methods, all producing identity_providers rows pointing at the same identity_id.

## Method 1: User self-links (primary method)

Both authentications happen in the same browser session. Proves control of both accounts simultaneously. No admin required, no email correlation, cryptographically sound.

Flow:
  1. Alice is logged in via LF SSO (session has identity_id=alice)
  2. She navigates to account settings → Link another identity
  3. She initiates OAuth flow for GitHub
  4. GitHub returns token with sub=github-12345
  5. stoa sees current session identity_id=alice + new (issuer=github, sub=github-12345)
  6. INSERT into identity_providers (identity_id=alice, issuer=github, sub=github-12345, linked_by='user-confirmed', linked_via_session=current_session_id)
  7. Future GitHub logins resolve to alice's identity_id

## Method 2: Admin asserts (operational fallback)

Admin API call linking two existing identity_providers records to the same identity_id. Used for bulk migration, legacy account merges, or when user self-linking is not possible. Full audit trail required — admin sub recorded in linked_by.

## Method 3: SCIM + email auto-link (managed IdPs only)

When SCIM provisions a user with email=alice@linuxfoundation.org and a login via another managed-tier provider also presents email=alice@linuxfoundation.org, auto-link if both sides are managed tier and email is foundation-issued. Never auto-link across trust tiers or with self-reported emails.

## Trust asymmetry — linking does not elevate

Session trust level is determined by which provider was used for THIS authentication, not by what is linked to the identity. Alice linking GitHub to her LF SSO identity does not make her GitHub sessions managed-tier. Hardware > managed > verified > federated applies per-session per-authentication.

## Schema addition

  ALTER TABLE identity_providers ADD COLUMN
      linked_via_session TEXT;  -- session id that performed the link; NULL for SCIM/admin

## API endpoints

  POST /account/link-provider
    → initiates OAuth flow for new provider
    → on callback: verify state param, extract issuer+sub from new token
    → check new provider not already linked to a DIFFERENT identity_id (conflict error)
    → INSERT identity_providers row
    → return updated provider list

  DELETE /account/link-provider/{issuer}/{sub}
    → unlink a provider from current identity
    → blocked if: last provider of any tier (no login method would remain)
    → blocked if: last managed-tier provider AND identity has managed-tier mailbox grants
       → requires admin to perform instead, with explicit reason
    → audit log row on every unlink

  POST /admin/identities/{identity_id}/link-provider (admin method 2)
    → admin asserts link without OAuth ceremony
    → records linked_by='admin', granted_by=admin_sub

## Conflict handling

If the new provider token resolves to an identity_providers row already linked to a DIFFERENT identity_id:
  → if other identity is inactive: admin can merge, user cannot
  → if other identity is active: hard conflict, requires admin resolution
  → never silently merge two active identities

## Orphan prevention

Cannot unlink last managed-tier provider if identity has any mailbox_grants on managed-tier mailboxes. System returns 409 with list of affected mailboxes. Admin must either: reassign those grants, downgrade mailbox min_trust_level, or explicitly force-unlink with reason recorded in audit log.
notes:
Identity ID is UUIDv7 — assigned by stoa at first contact (SCIM or first login), stable forever, not derived from any IdP attribute.

DID linking: when DID support is added, the linking ceremony for DIDs follows the same pattern as IdP provider linking but uses a DID challenge-response instead of OAuth. Flow:
  1. Alice is logged in (has active session with UUIDv7 identity_id)
  2. She initiates 'Link a DID' from account settings
  3. stoa generates a random challenge nonce
  4. Alice signs the nonce with her DID's private key
  5. stoa resolves the DID document, verifies the signature
  6. On success: INSERT into identity_dids (identity_id=alice, did=did:key:z6Mk...)

Same trust asymmetry applies: linking a DID does not change session trust level. DID trust tier TBD when implementing — did:key with hardware key storage could qualify as hardware tier; did:web is at most verified.

Same orphan prevention applies: cannot unlink last managed/hardware credential if managed mailboxes depend on it.

Conflict handling: a DID already linked to a different active identity_id is a hard conflict requiring admin resolution — same as IdP provider conflict.
title: design: identity linking ceremony — multi-provider same-person assertion
